feedback.worked_solution:
To compute ${f}^{′}(-2),$ we need to find the slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ at $x=-2.$

Let's consider the graph of $y=f(x)$ for $x\in [-5,0].$ Notice that $x=-2$ lies in this interval.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934289/assets/2f46cbe001623cacc7e7ae8f54d73f2bbc9ce685a9f75ffa93d78a9c621722fe.png)

The slope of $y=f(x)$ on $x\in (-5,-1)$ is constant and equals

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{-2-3}{-1-(-5)}=\frac{-5}{4}=-1.25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(-2)=-1.25.$
